context.// deployRuntime: THE cost control, and it defaults to false on purpose. When false, both ECS services synth with desiredCount 0 and the GPU ASG with min/max/desired all 0, so `cdk deploy` cannot start GPU spend. Turning it on is a deliberate act with a typed confirmation in the workflow (rules.md R-29) — never a default, never inherited from an environment variable. Verify with `npm run synth:check-zero` BEFORE deploying, not after.
context.// region: ap-south-1 only. CloudFront ACM certificates and AWS Budgets are global services that must live in us-east-1 — that is the documented exception, and it is the ONLY one (aws-setup-instructions.md §0.2).
context.// monthlyBudgetUsd: Placeholder until H-3 records the actual credit balance. A budget threshold with no cost baseline behind it is a number, not a control.
context.// budgetAlertEmail: Set before deploying CostSafetyStack. An unsubscribed SNS topic makes the Lambda the only backstop, and the Lambda is a DELAYED control (Budgets evaluates on a lag of hours) — nobody finds out until the money is spent.
context.// gatewayImageDigest: Promotion is by image DIGEST, not by rebuild (rules.md R-51, R-56). Tags are immutable in ECR, but a digest is the only thing that cannot be re-pointed at all. Left empty here: CI passes it with --context, and an empty value makes ComputeStack fail loudly rather than deploy :latest.
context.// allowedOrigins: Comma-separated EXACT origins, no wildcards. Empty on purpose: this is filled in on the SECOND pass, after EdgeStack has produced a CloudFront domain. ComputeStack cannot read that domain itself — EdgeStack depends on ComputeStack's Gateway service, so the reference would be a cycle. Empty is the safe state: the Gateway's origin validator rejects an empty allow-list and the process REFUSES TO BOOT, so forgetting the second pass yields a container that will not start rather than a Gateway that accepts every origin.
context.// jwtIssuer: The real identity provider's issuer URL. Must NOT be the local test issuer: a no-password JWKS issuer is a demo harness, not authentication, and the Gateway refuses to start if it sees one under the aws-gpu profile (rules.md R-05). Empty here so that an unconfigured deploy fails rather than silently trusting something.
context.// gitCommit: Stamped into the parity set and every audit row so a recorded decision can be tied to the code that made it. CI passes the real SHA; `unknown` is the honest fallback, because a fabricated commit on an audit row is worse than an absent one — it looks checkable.
context.// @aws-cdk/core:defaultCrossStackRefere: Set explicitly to `strong` rather than left to default, which silences a synth warning and — more usefully — locks in producer-protecting behaviour: CloudFormation refuses to delete an exported resource that another stack still imports. With five chained stacks that is the property worth having, because it turns `cdk destroy NetworkStack` while ComputeStack is alive into a clean refusal instead of a broken VPC. Migrating to `weak` is a three-step dance (both → deploy everywhere → weak) with no benefit here.
context.// @aws-cdk/core:checkSecretUsage: Fails synth if a Secrets Manager value is interpolated somewhere it would land in plaintext in the template — an automated form of rules.md R-34.
